added_claim_errors: Says a lost bank card is no obstacle because the bank can look up the account by ID card: unverifiable, no source given.
Says waiver of inheritance must be signed in person and cannot be delegated: unverifiable, stated flatly.
Says a 200-yuan minimum fee per case is common at notary offices: plausible, but not confirmed for any specific office.
Says a copy of the notarial certificate costs about 10 yuan: unverifiable, no source.

Cites an August 2026 ce.cn report, a State Council notice for 12378, and a Zhuanglang County notary fee page: I could not open the ce.cn and State Council pages (504 and socket error) and did not open the Zhuanglang page, so these are unverified.
Says some regions use an undertaking-based (gaozhi chengnuo) system for some certificates: unverifiable.
Advises both of them to go because the branch may require heirs to attend: unsupported, and it blurs the point that one heir is enough.

States the 2% rate as the 1998 national standard with a 200-yuan minimum: this checks out on the Guangdong page (Jijiafei 1998 No. 814). But B treats it as a calculation option and never tells the person the bank's 2% is wrong, which conflicts with the key's 'no 2% in the official standard'.

reasons: Both open by correcting the premise, cite Jin Gui [2024] No. 6, the 5万元 threshold summed per bank, and the four materials. I checked the 5万元 limit (unsettled interest excluded), the 18号文 article 4 materials and article 1 (no notarization rule) against gov.cn, and both match. A is firmer and more accurate on the key points: it says the mother alone can handle it, mentions the old 1万元 threshold, and gives the escalation path of bank customer service then 12378. It also says 2% is not a uniform national fee and lands on 100 to 200 yuan, close to the key's 200 yuan cap. B hedges with 大概率, recommends both go to the bank without saying one heir suffices, and presents 2% as a legitimate old national rate in a long table. It also adds the marital-property split and the 副本费, which makes it longer. B's 1998 2% claim is actually true, so the key's 'no 2%' is a little off, but B still never rejects the bank's 2% figure. A is shorter and cleaner, though both pad with the notary backup list.
